candidate.answerReason: Two legs per head accounts for every chicken and two of each cow's legs. Each cow contributes two extra legs, so there are 14/2 = 7 cows.

methods.label: Start with two legs per animal
methods.explanation:
Imagine first that every animal is a chicken. Since each animal has one head, this would give exactly twice as many legs as heads.

Replacing an imagined chicken with a cow leaves the head count unchanged but adds \(4-2=2\) legs. All \(14\) extra legs must come from cows, so the number of cows is
\[
14\div2=7.
\]
The answer is \(7\), choice B.
methods.levelReason: Uses the elementary all-chickens assumption and whole-number division.

candidate.annotationRationale: The problem directly targets the heads-and-legs assumption method described by cnm_p131. Division interprets the excess legs as groups of two, one group per cow.

review.mathematicalCheck: The two-leg baseline contributes twice the head count. Each cow adds exactly two legs, so the excess of 14 determines seven cows regardless of the chicken count.
review.levelCheck: The arithmetic baseline argument is accessible and complete.
